action_context_hypothesised_benefit: IPOTESI: reduce fast AMPA/kainate transmission by a measured fraction in the neuron-specific Wwox-deleted slice to ask whether spontaneous bursts need AMPAR current; competing explanations kept: NMDAR-regenerative burst, general loss of drive, state or recording condition, kainate contribution.
compound_or_probe: NBQX (competitive agonist-site antagonist; class knowledge, not read in a primary text)
identity_status: unresolved (no primary paper naming the compound or salt was reached; Harness is checking the catalogue; the abstracts spell the name out as 2,3-dihydroxy-6-nitro-7-sulfamoyl-benzo[f]quinoxaline); later: Chalupnik 2022 uses 'NBQX' with no salt or source stated
documented_action_and_limits: DATO (abstract only): no activity at NMDA and glycine sites (Sheardown 1990) and high-affinity binding to AMPA receptors only (Potschka 1998, rat binding). DATO (Digby discussion, text read): NBQX and CNQX also block kainate receptors. Not verified: potency, kainate window, slice kinetics, washout, salt, surmountability numbers. INFERENZA: a competitive block weakens when glutamate rises, as inside a burst; a gating modulator also changed NBQX 1 uM block in culture (abstract, Yamada 1996). UPDATE (Chalupnik 2022, partial_fulltext_read, recombinant rat, sf9 membranes, 4 C): DATO Ki 0.077 uM GluA2, 2.6/5.4/3.4 uM GluK1/2/3, 152 uM GluK5, so a binding window of about 34- to 70-fold over GluK1-3 (INFERENZA arithmetic); functional IC50, surmountability and glycine-site action were not measured there and stay abstract-level.
functional_comparison: INFERENZA: matched to d-APV (also surmountable) the pair shares one weakness, so a coincident curve cannot be read as equal need; matched to a noncompetitive tool it does not (decision 2 of A1).
mechanism_discriminating_control: IPOTESI: the independent partner of a noncompetitive tool, because its site (agonist site) differs from the collar pocket (D04); a noncompetitive-versus-competitive pair is the only AMPA pair in the module that is two mechanisms.
measurement_that_makes_it_interpretable: IPOTESI: fast-EPSC block fraction and time to steady state, NMDAR EPSC at the working concentration (the glycine-site and kainate statements rest on abstracts), intrinsic properties, burst readout under the verified block; stated as variables.
outcome_favourable: IPOTESI: bursts persist under a verified near-complete block (removes the AMPA-led reading for this preparation); with d-APV added only if bursts persist (order BE4).
outcome_contrary: IPOTESI: bursts abolished: expected under NMDAR-regenerative and general-drive explanations as well (AMPA block removes the depolarisation that relieves Mg2+ block); not a separating result. UPDATE: IPOTESI: at a working concentration near ten times the GluA2 Ki the GluK1-3 occupancy by binding Ki would still be low, so the arm could be named AMPA with a stated caveat (binding at 4 C does not transfer to a slice); measured kainate component in the preparation still decides (M-A5).
outcome_unresolved: IPOTESI: persistence at a partial block; abolition with an unmeasured NMDAR or glycine-site action of the tool; AMPA versus kainate unseparated because NBQX does not separate them (Digby discussion).
explanations_not_separated: NMDAR-regenerative burst with AMPAR-supplied depolarisation; presynaptic versus postsynaptic loss; kainate-receptor contribution (not separated); general loss of drive.
source_locator_depth: Sheardown 1990 and Potschka 1998 (abstracts via PubMed, abstract_only); Digby 2017 Discussion 4.6 (partial_fulltext_read); primary NBQX paper not reached: Sheardown page returned a bot check, not retried.; Chalupnik 2022 Table 1 (partial_fulltext_read). Primary text on surmountability and glycine site: not found open (queries Q16-Q20).
public_or_new_measurement: new measurement (NBQX selectivity and kinetics in the preparation); public literature supplies a class statement only

action_context_hypothesised_benefit: IPOTESI: same question with a noncompetitive 2,3-benzodiazepine, whose block is not surmounted by raised glutamate (voltage independent, activation not required: D02) and whose kainate window is reported as narrower (cited in Gangwar Introduction, not measured there).
compound_or_probe: GYKI 53655 (the compound the slice papers and the Yelshanskaya structure actually use); GYKI 52466 is the prototype the earlier package carried for kinetics
identity_status: name_mismatch (INFERENZA: the earlier package's probe row names GYKI 52466 and carries k_on 1.6e5 per M per s, k_off 3.2 per s from a citing paper, while every slice and structure datum read here is for GYKI 53655 / 'GYKI-53655' / 'GYKI53655'; Harness decides the catalogue match, names in names_used.tsv)
documented_action_and_limits: DATO: IC50 14.5 uM (recombinant GluA2, 3 mM Glu, -60 mV; cyclothiazide present in some experiments of the same paper) and 2.5 uM on the evoked slice EPSC; 10 uM blocked 80.5 percent (mEC) and 89 percent (barrel cortex L5) of the evoked peak, so not near-complete (Digby, Yelshanskaya). DATO: reversible, dose-dependent in the cingulate slice at 33-34 C with stepped applications of about 10 min (Dominguez-Sala). DATO (abstract only): block reduced from 84 to 38 percent by cyclothiazide and slower onset (Yamada). Not read in a primary text: NMDA and GABA-A inactivity (Donevan 1993) and the 2,3-benzodiazepine window (Bleakman 1996), both unreached; no concurrent EPSC verification with a burst readout in any paper read.
functional_comparison: INFERENZA: GYKI 53655 is noncompetitive and d-APV competitive, so a matched-effect comparison is between unlike tools; a coincident curve is then less likely to reflect a shared surmountability artefact.
mechanism_discriminating_control: IPOTESI: a noncompetitive tool is the verified-block tool; perampanel is not a second independent mechanism next to it (same collar pocket, D01, D04).
measurement_that_makes_it_interpretable: IPOTESI: block fraction on fast EPSC and mEPSC in the burst-recording medium, time course to steady state at slice temperature, NMDAR EPSC at a depolarised potential with the tool, intrinsic properties, a repeated-stimulation test of the block fraction (gating state, D12).
outcome_favourable: IPOTESI: bursts persist at a block above about 90 percent measured in the same medium (the Digby barrel-cortex evoked Up states persisted at 89 percent; spontaneous bursts untested).
outcome_contrary: IPOTESI: bursts abolished: as for C1, not separating AMPAR-led from NMDAR-regenerative drive; the Digby Up-state result, where d-APV but not GYKI-53655 abolished evoked Up states, would favour the NMDAR-regenerative reading in that preparation (transfer, evoked).
outcome_unresolved: IPOTESI: 80-90 percent block leaves residual AMPA current; the tool's NMDAR neutrality in the preparation is unmeasured (Donevan unreached); kainate window unquantified in a primary text read.
explanations_not_separated: Same four as C1 for AMPA versus NMDAR; plus AMPA versus kainate unresolved until the window is measured.
source_locator_depth: Yelshanskaya 2016 (partial_fulltext_read); Digby 2017 (partial_fulltext_read, Fig 5 viewed); Dominguez-Sala 2022 (partial_fulltext_read, Fig 6 viewed); Yamada 1996 (abstract_only); Donevan 1993 and Bleakman 1996 not_reached.
public_or_new_measurement: partly public (kinetics and a slice block fraction in a different region and age bracket), the rest new measurement (M-A1 to M-A5)

action_context_hypothesised_benefit: IPOTESI: perampanel as the reference noncompetitive tool already read in culture, to test whether the second noncompetitive AMPA tool agrees with the first (agreement across tools at one site is not independent confirmation).
identity_status: unresolved (named 'perampanel' or 'PMP' in every paper read; Gangwar lists a vendor catalogue number; Yelshanskaya states an Eisai gift; Harness decides the catalogue match)
documented_action_and_limits: DATO: IC50 0.89 uM on GluA2 (Yelshanskaya), 0.4-1.2 uM in culture (earlier package, reused), 58 uM on homomeric GluK2 (Gangwar); NMDA 10 and 100 uM currents unchanged by 30 uM in culture (reuse); onset tau 1.2 s and recovery tau 3.3 s in culture; DATO (abstract only): inhibits GluK5-containing kainate receptors at AMPA-comparable concentrations (Taniguchi). Not measured: slice kinetics, washout or verification; the Hanada displacement paper (noncompetitive tools displace perampanel binding, per its abstract) was not reached.
functional_comparison: INFERENZA: perampanel and GYKI 53655 are two compounds at one site: agreement between them tests the compound, not the mechanism; a disagreement would point to site-external actions or to a kainate difference.
mechanism_discriminating_control: IPOTESI: use perampanel as a same-site cross-check of the 2,3-benzodiazepine arm and, if its slow culture kinetics hold in the slice, as the arm where washout is least certain (unblock tau about 3 s in culture; tissue unmeasured); NBQX remains the independent mechanism.
measurement_that_makes_it_interpretable: IPOTESI: block fraction and steady-state time of perampanel in the slice; an occlusion test (perampanel after saturating GYKI 53655 adds no block if the site is one: M-A6); the kainate window in the preparation.
outcome_favourable: IPOTESI: perampanel and GYKI 53655 give the same persistence or abolition at matched measured block.
outcome_contrary: IPOTESI: perampanel abolishes bursts that GYKI 53655 spares at the same measured block (site-external or kainate action).
outcome_unresolved: IPOTESI: no tissue kinetics; GluK5-containing receptors not excluded in layer II/III.
explanations_not_separated: Same as C2; the pair adds no independent mechanism.
source_locator_depth: Yelshanskaya 2016, Gangwar 2023 (partial_fulltext_read; Gangwar Fig 4 viewed); Chen 2014 reused from the earlier staged receipt; Taniguchi 2022 abstract_only; Hanada 2011 not_reached (Wiley page returned a bot check, not retried).
public_or_new_measurement: partly public (culture and recombinant data), tissue part new measurement
